text.p: These are the leading stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nine convicted robbers executed by firing squad in southwest Nigerian city of Ibadan.
- Failure by government to develop maritime trade cost Nigeria over 100 million naira in revenue between January and June this year, Guardian investigation shows.
- A total 99 billion naira from estimated 189 billion naira has been released from 1997 budget for Nigerian states in first half of this year.
- State-run Nigerian Maritime Authority plans that vessels berthing at country's ports pass stringent security checks for safety purposes.
- Government mulls national policy on AIDS, to control increasing spread. Popular Nigerian maverick musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti recently died of AIDS-related causes.
- Multi-million naira World Bank project aimed at supplying drinking water to Lagos residents is threatened by environmental pollution from burst pipelines belonging to state oil company NNPC.
